title: Closures that remember
description:
Write functions that build and accept closures.

```
add_five(10) = 15
counter: 1 2 3
applied twice: 40
filtered: [12, 30, 48]
```
hints: `move |x| x + n` takes `n` into the closure, so it still exists after `make_adder` returns (lesson 5.01).
A counter changes what it captured, so it is `FnMut`: `let mut count = 0; move || { count += 1; count }`.
requirements: `fn apply_twice<F: Fn(i32) -> i32>(f: F, x: i32) -> i32`.
Filter a vector with a closure that captures a threshold.
stretch: Write `fn compose<A, B, C>(f: impl Fn(A) -> B, g: impl Fn(B) -> C) -> impl Fn(A) -> C`.
